prompt_text:
The figure summarizes several therapeutic strategies aimed at reducing vascular inflammation by targeting different immune-cell pathways. Across the top, monocyte recruitment to endothelial cells is shown as being driven by the CCR2–CCL2 axis and by integrin-mediated adhesion; these steps can be interrupted by CCR2 antagonism or by blocking signalling with Ac2-26. It also highlights neutrophil–platelet interactions at the vessel wall, where mediators such as CCL5, CXCL4, and DEFA1 appear to promote leukocyte activation, and suggests that preventing receptor heteromerization can disrupt this crosstalk.

The lower panels extend this concept to other inflammatory mechanisms. One shows neutrophil extracellular trap formation, with PAD4, gasdermin pores, histones, granule proteins, and extracellular DNA as targets for inhibitors, antibodies, or DNase. Another depicts dendritic cell–T cell–macrophage communication, where blocking co-stimulatory molecules like CD80/86 or inhibiting TRAF6 reduces NF-κB signalling and downstream chemokine and cytokine production. The final panel focuses on inflammation resolution: lipid mediators including resolvins, lipoxin A4, Ac2-26, and chemerin C15 act through receptors such as FPR2 and CMKLR1 to enhance efferocytosis of apoptotic cells and lower inflammatory cytokines. Overall, the image presents a coordinated map of anti-inflammatory intervention points.
